the_correction.the_same_defect_was_fixed_in_publish_too: `publish` had the identical fixed `.tmp` name. The review named `create`; fixing only the case and not the class is the mistake I have been caught making repeatedly, so both go through `_owned`.
the_correction.the_temporary_is_OWNED_before_it_is_writ: `instance._owned` creates it with `tempfile.mkstemp` in the selector's own parent -- O_EXCL, a regular file, a name nobody else holds -- and writes through that descriptor. A pre-existing entry at any other name is neither followed, truncated, reused nor removed: an unknown entry is somebody else's. Only this attempt's temporary is cleaned up.
the_correction.what_was_kept: the final-name no-clobber (`os.link`, which fails rather than replaces), atomic arrival by rename in `publish`, the pinned source digest and identity, and every earlier custody rule.
the_correction.what_was_wrong: `instance.create` wrote a FIXED `instance.json.new`, so it wrote through whatever was already at that name -- before the final name was ever considered. A symlink there redirected the write into a foreign document and published a SYMLINK as the selector; a hardlink to an existing selector destroyed that selector's bytes while publication went on to refuse and say it had left them alone.

the_lifecycle_takes_an_instance_path.a_verbs_options_follow_the_verb: `stack_command._stack` split the instance/root selection from the rest instead of appending the verb to everything, because argparse reads a subcommand's options only after the subcommand -- `monitor --interval 5` would otherwise have been unparseable. The four older verbs dispatch exactly as before, which is its own check.
the_lifecycle_takes_an_instance_path.how_the_command_is_found: v12/python/tools/instance.py `main`: `python3 -m tools.instance command <instance.json>` validates the selector and prints the installed command. Deriving it in shell would have been a second copy of `layout`.
the_lifecycle_takes_an_instance_path.recipes: v12/justfile: `bootstrap INPUTS DESTINATION DISTRO` forwards --destination/--distro when a destination is named; `start`, `stop`, `status` and `monitor` take an optional INSTANCE and, when given one, run THAT deployment's own command out of its own distro -- not this checkout's interpreter and not its sources. Without it, the older exported-operand form is unchanged.
the_lifecycle_takes_an_instance_path.runbook: v12/STACK.md: installing to a destination, the four instance-path commands, the same program without `just`, what the selector is validated against, and that the older form still works.
the_lifecycle_takes_an_instance_path.the_installed_monitor: v12/python/tools/stack.py `monitor`, registered in `stack_command.COMMANDS`. It derives the snapshot from `snapshot_path` -- the same answer `publish` and `status` use -- instead of the recipe rebuilding it from an environment variable, and refuses by name when nothing has been published.
